title: ERCLIP: Small-Data Adaptation of CLIP for Free-Length Image-Text Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2610.29939v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: CLIP's 77-token text encoder truncates detailed image descriptions. We present ERCLIP, a small-data adaptation of CLIP for long-caption image--text retrieval. During training, a long caption is split into sentences that the CLIP text encoder encodes independently; the sentence embeddings are fused by mean pooling or a gated residual Transformer scorer and receive their own contrastive loss. At inference ERCLIP is an unmodified CLIP dual encoder: test captions are still read through the 77-token window, and only training sees the full caption. We find that this fine-tuning erodes CLIP's zero-shot classification, most when the fusion output is not a combination of CLIP embeddings, and add a frozen-CLIP preservation loss on the image and short-caption embeddings. With 20k pairs and one epoch, ERCLIP improves long-caption R@1 over CLIP by 6.5--11.2 points, closing 62--77% of the gap to LongCLIP with 2% of its long captions. Preservation reco

translated_title: ERCLIP：面向自由长度图文检索的CLIP小数据适配方法
translated_abstract: CLIP的77个token文本编码器会截断详细的图像描述。我们提出了ERCLIP，一种面向长文本描述图文检索的CLIP小数据适配方法。在训练过程中，长文本描述被拆分成句子，由CLIP文本编码器独立编码；句子嵌入通过均值池化或门控残差Transformer评分器进行融合，并拥有各自的对比损失。在推理阶段，ERCLIP是一个未经修改的CLIP双编码器：测试时的文本描述仍通过77个token的窗口读取，只有训练阶段才能看到完整的文本描述。我们发现这种微调会损害CLIP的零样本分类能力，尤其是当融合输出不是CLIP嵌入的组合时更为严重，因此我们在图像嵌入和短文本描述嵌入上添加了冻结CLIP保留损失。仅使用2万个图文对和一个epoch的训练，ERCLIP在长文本检索R@1指标上比CLIP提升了6.5至11.2个百分点，以LongCLIP仅2%的长文本数据量弥补了与其62%至77%的性能差距。
tldr: ERCLIP通过将长文本描述拆分为句子独立编码并融合，仅在训练阶段使用完整长文本进行对比学习，配合冻结CLIP保留损失维持零样本分类能力，仅用2万图文对就将长文本图文检索R@1提升6.5至11.2个百分点，以LongCLIP 2%的数据量弥补其62%至77%的性能差距。
en_tdlr: ERCLIP adapts CLIP for long-caption image-text retrieval by splitting long captions into independently encoded, fused sentences with contrastive loss during training only, and with a frozen-CLIP preservation loss, it improves long-caption R@1 by 6.5-11.2 points using just 20k pairs, closing 62-77% of the gap to LongCLIP with 2% of its long captions.
